points.heading: Simple tenses
points.body:
Simple indicative tenses name a time without haber: present (canto), imperfect (cantaba), preterite (canté), future (cantaré), conditional (cantaría).

Each ending sits on the same stem idea: you change the tip to move the action in time. Example with cantar (I): canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría.

Práctica: Conjugate one -ar, one -er, and one -ir verb in I-form for the five simple tenses. Say out loud which time each form shows.

Error común: Mixing imperfect and preterite (using cantaba when the action is a finished event → canté).

points.heading: Compound tenses
points.body:
A compound tense uses two parts: an auxiliary verb (usually forms of haber) plus a past participle (often ending in -ado / -ido). The participle stays the same; the auxiliary changes for the person.

Examples: he cantado (I have sung), había comido (I had eaten), habrá vivido (will have lived). Think: helper verb + done-form of the main verb.

Práctica: Write five compound forms with the same participle (cantado or comido) using he / había / hube / habré / habría. Circle the auxiliary and underline the participle.

Error común: Changing the participle by person (hemos comidos). The participle does not take plural -s here.

lesson.summary: Master the ten indicative tenses: five simple (present, imperfect, preterite, future, conditional) and five compound with auxiliary + participle, knowing when to choose each.
